mainTopic: Partial הפרה of a woman's נזירות: אין נזירות לחצאין and אין קרבן לחצאין
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about a woman who took a נדר of נזירות: if her husband cancelled it without her knowing, she gets no מלקות even when she drinks wine. The גמרא uses this to challenge the view that a husband can cancel only the part of a vow that causes his wife suffering. Under that view, grape seeds and skins should stay forbidden and bring lashes. רב יוסף answers that נזירות cannot be split into parts. אביי rewords this as: neither נזירות nor its קרבן comes in halves. A ברייתא then challenges אביי: a woman whose נזירות was cancelled still brings a bird חטאת. The גמרא answers that a half-נזירות קרבן would need three animals, so the bird חטאת must come for another reason: a חטאת can be brought on a doubt. Finally, a new challenge against רבי יוחנן's rule of partial הפרה begins, using a woman who became טמא during her נזירות, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a woman's נזירות that her husband cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. A woman who breaks her נזירות gets מלקות. But if her husband cancelled it without her knowing, she gets no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A woman who vowed נזירות and drank wine or became טמא to the dead] gets the forty lashes. If her husband cancelled the vow but she did not know, and she drank wine or became טמא to the dead, she does not get the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא about a woman who was a נזירה. This sets up a challenge, in the next step, against the view that a husband can cancel only part of a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the vow stands, breaking it is a real איסור and she gets מלקות. Once the husband cancels it, the vow is gone, so she gets no מלקות even though she thought she was sinning. The key point for later is that the whole נזירות is gone, with no part of it left.

keyTerms.meaning: She receives the forty lashes (the punishment of מלקות)
He cancelled (a husband cancelling his wife's vow)
Becomes impure through a dead body, which a נזיר may not do
A woman who has taken a vow of נזירות

steps.confusionAlert: She gets no lashes even though she meant to sin. Once the husband cancels the vow, it no longer exists, so there is nothing for her to break.

phrases.english: she receives the forty lashes.
phrases.notes: We're starting in the middle of a ברייתא about a woman who vowed נזירות, then drank wine or became טמא to the dead.

phrases.english: If her husband cancelled [the vow] for her
and she did not know that he had cancelled it for her,
and she was drinking wine
or becoming impure through the dead —
she does not receive the forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵפֵר לָהּ בַּעְלָהּ וְהִיא לֹא יָדְעָה שֶׁהֵפֵר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted just before this section, in the discussion of partial הפרה.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא is cited to challenge, not to support, the view that a husband cancels only the part of a vow that causes suffering
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (used as a challenge): after הפרה, a נזירה gets no מלקות at all

steps.title: If cancellation is partial, she should still get lashes for seeds and skins
steps.stepSummary: Suppose a husband can only cancel the part of a vow that hurts his wife. Then here he cancelled only the wine. Grape seeds and skins would stay forbidden, and she should get מלקות for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he can cancel for the loaf that makes her suffer but not for the loaf that does not, then perhaps here he cancelled the wine, which pains her. He did not cancel the seeds and skins, since they do not pain her. Then she should get the forty lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack the view that a husband cancels only the painful part of a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is also forbidden to eat חרצן and זג, and giving those up causes her no real pain. If הפרה only covers the painful part, those איסורים should remain. Yet the ברייתא says she gets no מלקות at all, which suggests the whole vow was cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Causing her to suffer, to deny herself
Pain, suffering
Grape seeds
Grape skins
So she should receive (lashes)! This is the challenge

phrases.english: And if you say
he can cancel for the [loaf] that makes her suffer
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier case of two loaves, where only one of them would make her suffer.

phrases.english: but cannot cancel for the one that does not make her suffer,
then perhaps [the vow] from wine,
which causes her pain — he cancelled for her,

phrases.aramaic: מִן חַרְצָן וּמִן זַג — לֹא הֵפֵר לָהּ,
phrases.english: but from grape seeds and grape skins — he did not cancel for her,
since they cause her no pain.
So she should receive the forty lashes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מֵפֵר לַמִּתְעַנָּה וְאֵין מֵפֵר לְשֶׁאֵין מִתְעַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1 against partial הפרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a husband can cancel only the part of a vow that causes suffering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seeds and skins cause no pain, so they should stay forbidden and bring מלקות. But the ברייתא says she gets no lashes at all.

steps.title: רב יוסף: נזירות cannot be split
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that נזירות is different. It cannot exist in partial form, so cancelling any part cancels all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: There is no נזירות in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends partial הפרה by saying that נזירות is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary vows, a husband may cancel only the painful part. But נזירות is one package that cannot be split. Once the wine part is cancelled, the seeds and skins fall away too. So the ברייתא proves nothing about ordinary vows.

keyTerms.meaning: נזירות cannot exist in halves, in partial form

steps.whatToRemember: נזירות is all or nothing. Cancelling part of it cancels the whole thing.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
There is no naziriteship in halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֵין נְזִירוּת לַחֲצָאִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: נזירות is a special case and cannot be split, unlike ordinary vows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove that a husband always cancels a whole vow
steps.terutzMaskana: Only נזירות is all-or-nothing. Ordinary vows can still be cancelled in part.

steps.title: אביי objects to the wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רב יוסף's wording seems to suggest that a קרבן could be brought for half a נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does that mean there is a קרבן for half a נזירות?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is not rejecting רב יוסף's idea. He is challenging how it was worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying only 'there is no נזירות in halves' leaves room to think that the קרבן is different and could apply to partial נזירות. אביי sees that as wrong, so the wording needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering. A נזיר brings offerings, for example when his נזירות ends
There is, it exists

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But [does that mean] there is an offering for half a naziriteship?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָא קׇרְבָּן לַחֲצִי נְזִירוּת אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רב יוסף's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רב יוסף's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning only נזירות suggests that a קרבן could still apply to partial נזירות, which is not true.

steps.title: אביי's fuller wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי rewords the rule: neither נזירות nor its קרבן comes in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: There is no נזירות in halves, and there is no קרבן in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the corrected version of רב יוסף's rule. The next step challenges this new wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same: נזירות is all-or-nothing. אביי simply adds that the קרבן works the same way, so nobody reads the rule as allowing a קרבן for partial נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces the corrected version

steps.whatToRemember: Final wording: אין נזירות לחצאין ואין קרבן לחצאין. Both the נזירות and its קרבן are all-or-nothing, so הפרה of a נזירה wipes out everything.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
There is no naziriteship in halves,
and there is no offering in halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵין נְזִירוּת לַחֲצָאִין, וְאֵין קׇרְבָּן לַחֲצָאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the wording problem raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the rule to cover both נזירות and its קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's short wording suggested a קרבן might come for partial נזירות
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither נזירות nor its קרבן can be partial

steps.title: A ברייתא where she still brings a bird offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a woman whose husband cancelled her נזירות still brings a bird חטאת. That seems to show there is a קרבן for half a נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A woman vowed to be a נזיר and set aside her animal, and then her husband cancelled the vow. She brings a bird חטאת but not a bird עולה. If there is no קרבן for half a נזירות, why does she bring a bird חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's rule from step 5 using a ברייתא. In it, a woman who kept only part of her נזירות still brings some קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said there is no קרבן for half a נזירות. Here the woman's נזירות was cut short by her husband, so she kept only part of it. Yet the ברייתא says she brings a bird חטאת, which looks like a קרבן for half a נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
She set aside her animal for her קרבן
A bird sin-offering
A bird burnt-offering

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A woman who vowed to be a nazirite
and set aside her animal
and afterward her husband cancelled it for her,
brings a bird sin-offering,
but does not bring a bird burnt-offering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין קׇרְבָּן לַחֲצִי נְזִירוּת,
phrases.english: And if you say there is no offering for half a nazirite vow,
why does she bring a bird sin-offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reworded rule from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that there is no קרבן for half a נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman whose נזירות was cut short still brings a bird חטאת, so some קרבן does seem to come for a partial נזירות.

steps.title: A partial-נזירות offering cannot be the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if there really were a קרבן for half a נזירות, she would need all three animals of a נזיר, not just one bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that there is a קרבן for half a נזירות? Then she would need to bring three animals: a חטאת, an עולה, and a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the challenger's reading of the ברייתא cannot be right. This prepares the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If half a נזירות really got its own קרבן, it should be the regular נזיר set of three animals. The ברייתא only gives one bird. So the bird cannot be a 'half-נזירות קרבן', and some other reason must explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what would you say? (pushing back on the other option)
Peace-offering
She would need to bring

phrases.english: But rather, what?
Is there an offering for half a nazirite vow?
Then she would need to bring three animals:
a sin-offering, a burnt-offering, and a peace-offering!
phrases.notes: These are the three animals a נזיר brings when finishing a full נזירות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי יֵשׁ קׇרְבָּן לַחֲצִי נְזִירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the bird חטאת is a קרבן for half a נזירות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A real נזירות קרבן would be three animals, not one bird, so the bird cannot prove a half-נזירות קרבן.

steps.title: The bird חטאת comes because of doubt
steps.stepSummary: The rule stands: there is no קרבן for half a נזירות. The bird חטאת is brought for a different reason, because a חטאת can be brought in a case of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really there is no קרבן for half a נזירות. The bird חטאת she brings is because a חטאת can come when there is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6 and keeps אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת is not a 'half-נזירות קרבן'. A bird חטאת is a special קרבן that may be brought even when it is not certain one is obligated. So bringing it here does not prove anything about half a נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeping the original position)
A חטאת that can be brought in a case of doubt

steps.whatToRemember: There is no קרבן for half a נזירות. The one bird חטאת is explained by the special rule that a bird חטאת can be brought on a doubt.

phrases.english: Rather, really
there is no offering for half a nazirite vow.
And the bird sin-offering that she brings
is because a sin-offering can come in a case of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם אֵין קׇרְבָּן לַחֲצִי נְזִירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real explanation after step 7 ruled out the challenger's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case by a separate rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird חטאת looked like a קרבן for half a נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bird חטאת comes because a חטאת may be brought on a doubt, so אביי's rule stands.

steps.title: A new challenge from an impure woman's offering
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא is brought against רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband cancels only the part of a vow that causes suffering. It is about a woman who became impure during her נזירות. The question is only beginning here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: A woman vowed to be a נזיר, became impure, and afterward her husband cancelled the vow. She brings a bird חטאת but not a bird עולה. Now, if you say a husband cancels the part that causes suffering but not the part that doesn't...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge to the idea that a husband can only cancel what causes his wife suffering. The question is not finished on this amud; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the main rule behind the earlier steps: a husband cancels only the part of the vow that causes suffering. The ברייתא shows that after he cancels an impure woman's נזירות, she brings only the bird חטאת and not the bird עולה. The גמרא is about to ask how that fits if his cancelling only covers part of the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
She became impure
Causes herself suffering
Cancels (a vow)

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of a question. The punchline of the challenge comes on the next amud, so don't look for an answer yet.

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed at רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband only cancels the part that causes suffering.

phrases.english: A woman who vowed to be a nazirite and became impure,
and afterward her husband cancelled it for her,
brings a bird sin-offering,
and does not bring a bird burnt-offering.
And if you say he can cancel for the one that causes her suffering
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier case of the two loaves: he cancels for the loaf she'd suffer without, not the other.

phrases.english: but cannot cancel for the one that does not cause her suffering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the side question about half a נזירות, the גמרא returns to challenging the rule that step 2 attacked: that a husband cancels only the part of a vow that causes suffering
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband cancels only the part of a vow that causes suffering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the husband's cancelling as freeing her from the bird עולה. The challenge, still being set up, will ask how that fits if he only cancels part of the vow.
